headline: Leaving Verizon Dollars forfeits your balance and fee-free upgrades
tldr: Verizon's loyalty terms now spell out the cost of opting out: your Verizon Dollars are forfeited on the spot, and fee-free activations and upgrades end.
who: Verizon postpaid mobile, Home Internet and Fios customers enrolled in Verizon Dollars, Verizon's loyalty program, especially anyone who joined for the waived activation and upgrade fees or the Glance lock-screen rewards and is thinking of leaving
seo_title: Opting out of Verizon Dollars: you forfeit your balance and lose waived activation and upgrade fees
seo_desc: Verizon added section 7.4 to its Verizon Dollars terms: un-enrolling forfeits accumulated Dollars (except Verizon Visa Card earnings), voids refunds on items bought with Dollars and ends waived activation and upgrade fees.

redline.after: If you choose to opt out of Verizon Dollars, you agree: All accumulated Verizon Dollars will be immediately forfeited, with the exception of Verizon Dollars earned by Verizon Visa Card holders for eligible Verizon Visa Card spend.
redline.label: Verizon Dollars Terms · 7.4 Opt-Out
redline.note: Leaving the program now costs you whatever balance you haven't spent.

redline.after: You will lose access to waived fees for mobile device activations and/or upgrades.
redline.label: Verizon Dollars Terms · 7.4 Opt-Out
redline.note: Verizon's own newsroom puts those fees at up to $40 per device.

redline.after: Verizon purchases (e.g., accessories, devices) made with Verizon Dollars will be ineligible for a refund.
redline.label: Verizon Dollars Terms · 7.4 Opt-Out

actions: Before you opt out, spend your balance in the My Verizon app (Me tab, Verizon Dollars tile) on a gift card, accessory or device you want
If you bought something with Verizon Dollars and might return it, return it before you opt out: after that it can't be refunded
If you only want to stop the Glance lock-screen tracking, uninstall Glance instead of leaving Verizon Dollars; you keep your balance and the fee waivers
what:
Verizon has added a new section 7.4, "Opt-Out," to the Terms and Conditions of Verizon Dollars, the loyalty program that pays 3% of your monthly bill back in Verizon Dollars. It wasn't on the page on November 13; it is on November 14.

The section says you can unenroll "at any time via the opt-out link in the Verizon Dollars dashboard in the My Verizon App," but that if you do, "you agree" to four things:

- "All accumulated Verizon Dollars will be immediately forfeited, with the exception of Verizon Dollars earned by Verizon Visa Card holders for eligible Verizon Visa Card spend."
- "You will no longer earn Verizon Dollars for Verizon bill payments or other eligible offers like Lock Screen Rewards through Glance, if applicable."
- "Verizon purchases (e.g., accessories, devices) made with Verizon Dollars will be ineligible for a refund."
- "You will lose access to waived fees for mobile device activations and/or upgrades."

It adds that leaving "will not affect hotel or ticket rewards you have already redeemed" and that you "may re-enroll in the Program at any time via the My Verizon App." The terms don't say whether re-enrolling restores a forfeited balance.

## Why it matters

The waived fees are the main reason many customers joined. Verizon's newsroom post launching the program called it "the end of Device Upgrade and Activation fees" and put them at "up to $40 in fees per device," available only to customers who opt in. Section 7.4 makes clear the waiver lasts only as long as you stay enrolled. The terms already said Dollars are forfeited if you cancel Verizon service (7.3) or if Verizon ends your enrollment (7.2); now opting out of the program alone costs you the balance too.

It also matters for the Glance deal we covered on October 19: earning $5 a month in Lock Screen Rewards requires keeping "Do not sell or share my personal information" switched off. Customers who regret that and want out of Verizon Dollars entirely now see in writing that leaving forfeits what they earned. Uninstalling the Glance app ends Lock Screen Rewards without leaving Verizon Dollars, according to section 10.2.

What stays the same: you earn 3% of eligible bill payments, Dollars earned without a Verizon Visa Card still expire 12 months after they're issued, and Visa cardholders keep card-earned Dollars after opting out.

Verizon's Verizon Dollars FAQ (checked Nov 14) lists the same consequences under "Can I un-enroll from Verizon Dollars?" We don't know when that FAQ answer was added. The terms page still shows a placeholder, "effective as of <DATE>," so there is no stated effective date.
sources: Verizon Dollars Program: Terms and Conditions
About Verizon: Verizon breaks industry mold (loyalty program launch)
faq: What happens to my Verizon Dollars if I opt out?
Under section 7.4 of the program terms, all accumulated Verizon Dollars are forfeited immediately, except Dollars earned by Verizon Visa Card holders on eligible card spending.
Do I lose free activations and upgrades if I leave Verizon Dollars?
Yes. Section 7.4 says you "will lose access to waived fees for mobile device activations and/or upgrades." Verizon's launch announcement put those fees at up to $40 per device.
Can I rejoin later?
The terms say you may re-enroll at any time in the My Verizon app. They don't say a forfeited balance comes back.

headline: Hinge now uses OpenAI to analyze your chats, and may train its own models on your messages
tldr: Hinge's new Chat Insights runs your messages through OpenAI to make suggestions and personalize matches, and Hinge may train its models on them. There's a toggle in Settings.
who: Anyone who messages matches on Hinge, and the people they message, especially anyone who shares sensitive details (health, sexuality, location, plans to meet) in Hinge chat.
seo_title: Hinge Chat Insights: Hinge uses OpenAI on your messages. How to turn it off
seo_desc: Hinge's new help pages say Chat Insights uses OpenAI to look for patterns in your chats, and Hinge may use messages, sometimes raw, to train the models behind it. Settings > Chat Insights turns it off.

redline.after: Chat Insights helps us understand how your chats are going, so we can support you in the right moments. We use OpenAI to look for patterns and make suggestions that can help improve your experience.
redline.label: Help Center · What are Chat Insights? (new, Nov 9, 2026)
redline.note: Hinge's first OpenAI feature, Convo Starters, came with a promise that it does not process private messages. This one is built on them.

redline.after: This may include recommending other daters who we think better reflect your preferences, offering in-chat suggestions or feedback, tailoring features to your interests, or training the specific models behind these features.
redline.label: Help Center · How Does Hinge Use My Messages (new, Oct 28, 2026)
redline.note: Your messages can feed who Hinge shows you, and the models themselves.

redline.after: However, some use cases may require Hinge to process raw messages, which may include identifiable information or data considered sensitive under applicable law.
redline.label: Help Center · How Does Hinge Use My Messages
redline.note: Hinge says it will pseudonymize or de-identify "where possible", not always.

actions: To opt out, open Hinge, tap your photo icon, then Settings (the gear icon), scroll to Chat Insights and switch it off. Hinge's other page calls the same switch "Chat Insights for Personalization" in Account Settings
Check the switch even if you don't remember agreeing to anything: Hinge's pages don't say whether it starts on or off
Keep in mind that safety scanning and human review of chats aren't covered by the switch. Hinge says the only way to object to those is to delete your account
what:
Hinge has published two new help-center articles that describe a new use for your messages. "How Does Hinge Use My Messages" was created on October 28, 2026 and "What are Chat Insights?" on November 9, 2026, according to the help center's own timestamps. Both were last edited on November 13. Neither page existed in the Wayback Machine when we checked on November 14, and we found no news coverage.

## What Chat Insights does

The Chat Insights page says: "Chat Insights helps us understand how your chats are going, so we can support you in the right moments. We use OpenAI to look for patterns and make suggestions that can help improve your experience." It adds: "Hinge uses Chat Insights, but never shows them to other daters. Chat Insights improves Hinge over time. Patterns across conversations help us build features that make chatting feel easier."

The messages page explains what that personalization covers. "With your permission, we may also use the messages you send on Hinge to develop and test features designed to enable a more personalized experience for you on the app. This may include recommending other daters who we think better reflect your preferences, offering in-chat suggestions or feedback, tailoring features to your interests, or training the specific models behind these features."

It promises to keep the data to "the minimum necessary, including by pseudonymizing or de-identifying the messages where possible." Then it adds: "However, some use cases may require Hinge to process raw messages, which may include identifiable information or data considered sensitive under applicable law. If you'd rather this type of content never be used to personalize your experience, opting out is the simplest way to ensure that."

## Why it matters

Hinge's first OpenAI feature came with a different promise. When Convo Starters launched (Hinge newsroom, December 8, 2025), its help page said the feature uses only profile photos, Prompt answers and pronouns, and "Convo Starters do not analyze or otherwise process facial geometry, biometric data, or private messages." It also said OpenAI "cannot use the data to train its models, and deletes the data within 30 days of receipt." That page is still up. The Chat Insights pages name OpenAI, but they don't repeat those no-training and 30-day deletion terms or say whether they apply.

The pages also don't say whether Chat Insights starts switched on or off. "With your permission" suggests Hinge asks first, but neither page says how or when. Hinge's App Store release notes for its last two updates (10.12.1 and 10.12.2) only mention "performance improvements."

There's a second person in every chat. The messages page says: "Where and as legally required, Hinge will not process messages in a conversation unless all parties are opted in." That promise is limited to places where the law requires it. The page doesn't say what happens elsewhere when you have Chat Insights off and your match has it on.

Hinge's Privacy Policy (in effect since November 24, 2025, checked November 14) doesn't mention Chat Insights or OpenAI. It does already list "Developing and improving new features and services, including through machine learning" as a use of your data, and it counts "your chats with other members" among the content you share.

## What you can't turn off

The messages page lists uses of your chats that have no toggle: delivering them, "Safety and moderation: detecting harassment, scams, and other violations of our guidelines, whether by automated systems or human review", security, debugging, and aggregate analytics using de-identified or aggregated data. "If you object to Hinge's use of your messages for these purposes, you may delete your account." The Chat Insights page says turning the feature off "does not interfere with Hinge's safety processes."

## How other dating apps handle your messages

We checked what the other big dating apps say about AI and your chats (pages fetched November 14, 2026).

Grindr asks before training on chats. Its "Your Privacy & Artificial Intelligence at Grindr" help page counts "chat content" as special-category data and says: "You can choose whether or not to let Grindr use this type of data to train its AI technology. You'll see this option when you create your account." Its AI features, which include "summaries of previous interactions with other users" and "chat suggestions", are on "By default" until you opt out under "Enable gAI™ Features".

Bumble's Privacy Policy says it reviews "the content of messages sent in the App to identify topics, sentiments, and trends across our Users" after it will "take steps to remove personally identifying information from such messages, prior to reviewing them." It lists OpenAI as an AI provider for message prompts such as Icebreakers, noting OpenAI "only retains inputs and prompts for 30 days".

Tinder said in March 2026 that it gave its "Are You Sure?" and "Does This Bother You?" safety prompts "Large Language Model-powered upgrades" that read "tone and conversational nuance".

Hinge's pages say messages may be used, "With your permission", to train "the specific models behind these features", and that some uses "may require Hinge to process raw messages". Unlike Grindr's page, they don't say when or how that permission is asked. Unlike Hinge's own Convo Starters page and Bumble's policy, they don't state how long OpenAI keeps the data.

## What stays the same

Hinge says it "will never voluntarily share your messages with daters other than the intended recipients, nor with advertisers or other third-party companies aside from the approved service providers we engage to help us operate and improve the Hinge Service." You can still use chat with Chat Insights off.

What you can do: open Hinge, tap your photo icon, then Settings (the gear icon), scroll down to Chat Insights and toggle it off. The messages page calls the same switch "Chat Insights for Personalization" in Account Settings.
sources: Hinge Help Center: What are Chat Insights? (created Nov 9, 2026)
Hinge Help Center: How Does Hinge Use My Messages (created Oct 28, 2026)
Hinge Help Center: What are Convo Starters?
Hinge Newsroom: Hinge Launches Convo Starters (Dec 8, 2025)
Grindr Help Center: Your Privacy & Artificial Intelligence at Grindr
Tinder Press Room: Tinder Sparks 2026 keynote (Mar 12, 2026)
faq: Does Hinge use OpenAI on my messages?

For Chat Insights, yes. Hinge's help page says: "We use OpenAI to look for patterns and make suggestions that can help improve your experience." Hinge says the insights are never shown to other daters.
How do I turn off Chat Insights on Hinge?

Tap your photo icon, then Settings (gear icon), scroll to Chat Insights and toggle it off. Hinge's messages page calls it "Chat Insights for Personalization" in Account Settings. You can still use chat with it off.
Can Hinge train AI on my messages?

Hinge's own models, yes, if Chat Insights is on: its help page lists "training the specific models behind these features" as a use. The Chat Insights pages don't say whether OpenAI may keep or train on the data. For the older Convo Starters feature, Hinge said OpenAI can't train on the data and deletes it within 30 days.
Does turning off Chat Insights stop Hinge from scanning my chats?
No. Safety and moderation (automated and human review), security, debugging and aggregate analytics have no toggle. Hinge says if you object to those, you can delete your account.
Do other dating apps use AI on your messages?

Yes, in different ways. Grindr says you choose at sign-up whether it can train AI on chat content, but its AI features (including chat summaries) are on by default. Bumble reviews message content for topics and trends after removing personal details, and uses OpenAI for Icebreakers with 30-day retention. Tinder uses large language models in its "Are You Sure?" safety prompts.

headline: HunterSMART Google Home and Alexa cloud link ends Jan 1, 2027
tldr: From Jan 1, 2027, HunterSMART's legacy cloud link to Google Home and Alexa stops. The app and remote still work; Matter is only for eligible models.
who: Anyone who controls a HunterSMART ceiling fan through Google Home or Amazon Alexa by linking their HunterSMART account, especially owners of models that are not eligible for Matter
seo_title: HunterSMART Google Home and Alexa cloud link ends January 1, 2027
seo_desc: From January 1, 2027, Hunter ends the legacy cloud-to-cloud link between HunterSMART apps and Google Home or Alexa. Voice commands, scenes and automations that use that link stop. The app and remote still work; Matter is only for eligible models.

redline.after: Beginning January 1, 2027, Hunter will discontinue the legacy cloud-based connections that currently enable cloud-to-cloud linking between HunterSMART™ app accounts and Google Home and Amazon Alexa.
redline.label: Hunter blog · What Is Changing? (Nov 5, 2026)
redline.note: This is the official announcement, not only the customer email quoted in the press.

redline.after: After this date, Google Home and Alexa functionality that relies on this legacy cloud connection will no longer work for HunterSMART™ fans, including voice commands, scenes, and automations.
redline.label: Hunter blog · What Is Changing?

redline.after: Your fan's core operation will continue as designed, including fan and lighting control through the included remote control, other installed controls, and smart controls via the HunterSMART™ app, as applicable.
redline.label: Hunter blog · What Does This Mean for My HunterSMART™ Fan Controls?

actions: Check whether your fan is eligible for Matter on Hunter's Matter compatibility page, and complete any firmware or hardware upgrade and re-pairing before January 1, 2027

If your model is not eligible, plan to use the HunterSMART app and the included remote after that date: Google Home and Alexa voice commands, scenes and automations that used the old account link will stop
If you migrate to Matter, add the fan directly in the Google Home or Alexa app and recreate scenes and automations; the old HunterSMART account link will not carry them over
what:
Hunter, the ceiling-fan maker, is ending the legacy cloud link that connects HunterSMART fans to Google Home and Amazon Alexa. The official announcement, posted November 5, 2026 and fetched November 14, 2026, is clear about the date: "Beginning January 1, 2027, Hunter will discontinue the legacy cloud-based connections that currently enable cloud-to-cloud linking between HunterSMART™ app accounts and Google Home and Amazon Alexa." "After this date, Google Home and Alexa functionality that relies on this legacy cloud connection will no longer work for HunterSMART™ fans, including voice commands, scenes, and automations."

## What stays the same

The fan itself does not shut off. Hunter says: "Your fan's core operation will continue as designed, including fan and lighting control through the included remote control, other installed controls, and smart controls via the HunterSMART™ app, as applicable." If you already control the fan from the HunterSMART app or the remote in the box, that path is not what is being discontinued.

## Matter is only for eligible models

Hunter is moving eligible HunterSMART products to Matter. "If your fan is eligible for Matter compatibility, you will be able to continue using supported smart functionality within the Google Home and/or Alexa ecosystems after completing the applicable Matter migration and setup." After that, you no longer link your HunterSMART account to Google Home or Alexa. You add the fan directly in those apps using their Matter setup. "Matter-enabled devices do not use the legacy cloud-linking service for smart controls that is being discontinued."

Eligibility is not universal. Hunter's [Matter compatibility page](https://www.hunterfan.com/pages/matter) says the path "will vary depending on your fan model and hardware configuration" and that Matter "may require a firmware update or updated hardware components." Customers who do not complete an available migration "will no longer be able to use certain HunterSMART™ cloud-based smart-home features after the transition," though core operation through the remote or other installed controls continues. After a Matter migration you may need to add the fan as a new device and "recreate scenes, routines, automations, schedules, or other customized settings."

## What you can do

Look up your model on the Matter page and, if an upgrade is offered, finish it and re-pair the fan before January 1, 2027. If your fan is not eligible, treat the HunterSMART app and the included remote as the controls that will still work.

Coverage (checked November 14, 2026): [9to5Google](https://9to5google.com/2026/11/09/hunter-ceiling-fans-google-home-amazon-alexa-support/) reported the change on November 9, quoting a Hunter customer email that matches the official blog. Android Authority also noted the November 5 announcement.

Related: [Apps and devices that stop working Jan 1, 2027](../../guides/apps-and-devices-that-stop-working-jan-1-2027/).
sources: Hunter: Important Update to HunterSMART Google Home and Amazon Alexa Connectivity via App-to-App Linking (Nov 5, 2026)
Hunter: Matter Compatibility Updates for HunterSMART Fans
9to5Google: Hunter is killing Google Home, Alexa controls for its smart ceiling fans (Nov 9, 2026)
faq: When do HunterSMART Google Home and Alexa controls stop?

The legacy cloud-to-cloud account link ends January 1, 2027. Voice commands, scenes and automations that depend on that link stop on that date. Hunter's official blog, fetched November 14, 2026, is the source.
Will my Hunter ceiling fan still work?
Yes. Hunter says core operation continues, including the included remote, other installed controls, and the HunterSMART app.
Can I keep using Google Home or Alexa after January 1?

Only if your fan is eligible for Matter and you complete the migration and set the fan up directly in the Google Home or Alexa app. Matter is not offered for every model; check Hunter's Matter compatibility page.

headline: Noodoe app and cloud shut down worldwide on Jan 1, 2027
tldr: From Jan 1, 2027 the KYMCO Noodoe app will not launch and the cloud shuts down worldwide. On the dash, only the speed reading keeps working as normal.
who: Anyone who uses the KYMCO Noodoe app or the Noodoe-connected dash features on a KYMCO scooter, anywhere in the world
seo_title: KYMCO Noodoe app and cloud shut down worldwide January 1, 2027
seo_desc: KYMCO is discontinuing the Noodoe app and all associated cloud services on January 1, 2027, worldwide. The app will not launch. Navigation, messages, weather and gallery stop; only the speed reading keeps working as normal.

redline.after: Effective January 1, 2027, all services, functions, and technical support will be terminated worldwide.
redline.label: KYMCO USA · Noodoe System Discontinuation Notice (bulletin PU-2025-1219)

redline.after: The KYMCO Noodoe Application will no longer launch. Regardless of login status, users will be unable to access the App.
redline.label: KYMCO USA · Scope of impact

redline.after: Speed Display: This function will continue to operate normally (data comes directly from instrument panel).
redline.label: KYMCO USA · Scope of impact
redline.note: Clock time will still be shown but cannot be adjusted, because that calibration went through the app.

actions: Do not count on the Noodoe app, in-dash navigation, messages, weather or the gallery after January 1, 2027; the app will not launch and the cloud is shut down worldwide

If you still use in-dash navigation, save any routes or map details you need before that date; KYMCO already shortened map-data validity from three years to two, and map updates end when the app stops launching
Plan to use a phone or other GPS for navigation, and remember that the clock on the dash will still show the time but can no longer be adjusted through the app
what:
KYMCO is shutting down the Noodoe app and its cloud. In a notice on [kymcousa.com](https://kymcousa.com/kymco-noodoe-system-discontinuation/), marked as official product update bulletin PU-2025-1219 and dated December 19, 2025 (fetched November 14, 2026), the company says: "Effective January 1, 2027, all services, functions, and technical support will be terminated worldwide."

## What stops

The impact list is specific:

- "The KYMCO Noodoe Application will no longer launch. Regardless of login status, users will be unable to access the App."
- "The KYMCO Noodoe cloud services and servers will be permanently shut down."
- Navigation pages will not display.
- Message pages will not display.
- Weather data will no longer be displayed (it was "previously calibrated via the KYMCO App").
- Photos cannot be added or deleted in the gallery.

A separate map-policy note says that on February 27, 2025, KYMCO shortened the validity of navigation map data from three years to two, and that starting January 1, 2027, "the KYMCO App will no longer launch, and users will be unable to use navigation functions or update map data."

## What keeps working

"Speed Display: This function will continue to operate normally (data comes directly from instrument panel)." The clock will still show the time, but "cannot be adjusted (previously calibrated via the KYMCO App)." The scooter itself is not being discontinued; this notice is about the Noodoe application and cloud services.

## What you can do

If you rely on the in-dash navigation or anything stored in the app, copy it before January 1, 2027. After that date there is no app to open and no cloud to reach. Questions, the notice says, go to your designated KYMCO USA sales representative.

Coverage (checked November 14, 2026): we are citing KYMCO USA's own discontinuation page.

Related: [Apps and devices that stop working Jan 1, 2027](../../guides/apps-and-devices-that-stop-working-jan-1-2027/).
sources: KYMCO USA: KYMCO Noodoe System Discontinuation Notice (bulletin PU-2025-1219)
faq: When does KYMCO Noodoe shut down?
January 1, 2027, worldwide. That date is in KYMCO USA's discontinuation notice (bulletin PU-2025-1219), fetched November 14, 2026.
Will the scooter still show my speed?
Yes. KYMCO says the speed display will continue to operate normally because the data comes directly from the instrument panel. The clock will still show the time but cannot be adjusted.
Can I still open the Noodoe app after January 1, 2027?
No. The notice says the application will no longer launch, regardless of login status, and the cloud services and servers will be permanently shut down.

headline: Fresh & Save app shuts Dec 31, 2026; save your data first
tldr: The ZWILLING app, used with Fresh & Save, shuts December 31, 2026. After that you cannot log in. Vacuum boxes still work; save box contents, expiry dates and lists first.
who: Anyone who uses the ZWILLING app to track Fresh & Save boxes, expiry dates, shopping lists or other app-only features
seo_title: ZWILLING Fresh & Save app shuts December 31, 2026: save your data first
seo_desc: ZWILLING is discontinuing its app on December 31, 2026. From January 2027 you cannot log in. Fresh & Save products still work. Save box contents, expiry dates and shopping lists before the shutdown.

redline.after: we have made the strategic decision to discontinue the ZWILLING app by December 31, 2026.
redline.label: ZWILLING · FAQ App Discontinuation

redline.after: From January 2027, you will no longer be able to log in or use the app, so the app will not be usable.
redline.label: ZWILLING FAQ · Will I still be able to log in and use the app?
redline.note: That is true even if the app is still installed, and even offline.

redline.after: Customers should save or copy any information they still need before December 31, 2026.
redline.label: ZWILLING FAQ · Will the app continue to work if I already have it installed

actions: Before December 31, 2026, write down or screenshot the contents of your Fresh & Save boxes, estimated expiration dates, and any shopping list you still need; there is no substitute app for managing box contents
Keep proof of purchase and product identifiers for warranty or support questions; those are unchanged, and your zwilling.com account still works for shopping
Recipes and articles in the app move off the phone: use the Inspiration area on zwilling.com if you still want them
what:
ZWILLING is discontinuing its mobile app, which is the app Fresh & Save owners use for storage tracking and expiry reminders. In a [FAQ on zwilling.com](https://www.zwilling.com/us/magazine/faqs-app-exit.html), fetched November 14, 2026, the company says it has "made the strategic decision to discontinue the ZWILLING app by December 31, 2026." "Customers can continue using the app until December 31, 2026. From January 2027, the app will no longer be available, and app-based features and services will be deactivated."

## You will not be able to log in

"From January 2027, you will no longer be able to log in or use the app, so the app will not be usable." That is true even if the app is still on your phone, and even if you try to use it offline. It also leaves the App Store and Google Play: "From January 2027, the app will no longer be available for download or re-download from app stores." Scanning a QR or NFC code on a product or its packaging will no longer open the app or its features.

## What to save first

ZWILLING's own advice is to copy anything you still need before December 31, 2026. From January 2027 you will not see saved Fresh & Save boxes in the app, and you will not get expiry notifications. "We recommend writing down or taking a screenshot of the contents of your boxes and their estimated expiration dates before the app is discontinued." Shopping lists disappear too, so copy those as well. There is "currently no substitute solution for managing the content of the boxes or fridge."

Other app-only features that stop: shopping inside the app, product registration through the app, recipes and content articles in the app (recipes remain on zwilling.com in the Inspiration area), and push notifications.

## What stays the same

Fresh & Save is not being discontinued. "Your Fresh & Save products will continue to work as normal. All functions that do not rely on the app remain fully intact." Your customer account "will still be available for login and shopping on zwilling.com." Warranties and product support are unchanged.

Coverage (checked November 14, 2026): we are citing ZWILLING's official app-discontinuation FAQ.

Related: [Apps and devices that stop working Jan 1, 2027](../../guides/apps-and-devices-that-stop-working-jan-1-2027/).
sources: ZWILLING: Frequently asked questions — App Discontinuation
faq: When does the ZWILLING Fresh & Save app shut down?
You can use it through December 31, 2026. From January 2027 you cannot log in, even if the app is still installed. That is from ZWILLING's official FAQ, fetched November 14, 2026.
Will my Fresh & Save vacuum boxes still work?

Yes. ZWILLING says Fresh & Save remains in its portfolio and that all functions that do not rely on the app stay intact. Storage tracking, expiry notifications and shopping lists in the app are what go away.
What should I save before December 31?

ZWILLING recommends writing down or screenshotting the contents of your boxes and their estimated expiration dates, and copying your shopping list. There is currently no substitute app for managing box contents.

headline: MyPowerRouter.com and support end Dec 31, 2026
tldr: Nedap shuts MyPowerRouter.com on December 31, 2026, along with online monitoring, energy data, remote updates and all remaining support. The device's local screen still works; save your data first.
who: Anyone who still monitors a Nedap PowerRouter through MyPowerRouter.com, or who may need firmware updates, remote assistance or a new warranty claim after 2016 sales ended
seo_title: Nedap MyPowerRouter.com shuts December 31, 2026: monitoring, data and support end
seo_desc: Nedap will terminate MyPowerRouter.com on December 31, 2026. Online logins, energy data, remote software updates and remaining PowerRouter support end that day. The device's local screen still works. Save your data first.

redline.after: Nedap will terminate the MyPowerRouter.com environment as of 31 December 2026.
redline.label: Nedap · Termination of MyPowerRouter.com and PowerRouter Services as of 31 December 2026

redline.after: From that date onward, it will no longer be possible via MyPowerRouter.com to: log in; access system or energy data online; perform remote software updates; use any other online functionalities.
redline.label: Nedap · 1. Termination of the Online Service
redline.note: The notice lists those four items as bullets; the wording here is the notice's own phrases, joined for the redline.

redline.after: The local functionalities of the PowerRouter device itself, including the display of data via the integrated screen, will remain unchanged.
redline.label: Nedap · 1. Termination of the Online Service

actions: Download or otherwise save any system status, energy data or account records you still need from MyPowerRouter.com before December 31, 2026; Nedap advises users to secure required data by then, and accounts will later be deactivated and personal data deleted or anonymized
If you have a warranty issue, submit the claim in writing before December 31, 2026; Nedap will not accept new warranty claims after that date
After December 31, plan to read the unit from its integrated screen only: online monitoring, remote updates, technical support and remote assistance all end
what:
Nedap is closing the online portal for its PowerRouter energy system. On [powerrouter.com](https://www.powerrouter.com/en/discontinuation-mypowerrouter-com/), fetched November 14, 2026, the company says: "Nedap will terminate the MyPowerRouter.com environment as of 31 December 2026."

Nedap stopped selling the PowerRouter line in 2016 and kept the portal running for existing users. That extended period is now ending.

## What stops on December 31, 2026

From that date, it will no longer be possible via MyPowerRouter.com to:

- log in;
- access system or energy data online;
- perform remote software updates;
- use any other online functionalities.

The same date ends remaining service and support for the product line, including technical support, remote assistance, and firmware- or software-related support and updates. "After this date, Nedap will no longer provide any support or services relating to the PowerRouter or the MyPowerRouter environment."

Warranty claims "submitted in writing before 31 December 2026 will be handled in accordance with the applicable warranty terms." "No new warranty claims can be submitted after 31 December 2026."

## What stays the same

"This termination relates exclusively to the online services provided via MyPowerRouter.com. The local functionalities of the PowerRouter device itself, including the display of data via the integrated screen, will remain unchanged."

## What happens to your data

"Following termination of the service, user accounts will be deactivated. Any personal data processed within the framework of MyPowerRouter.com will be deleted or anonymized once it is no longer necessary for the purpose for which it was collected," in line with GDPR and applicable retention periods. "We advise users to secure any required data before 31 December 2026."

Coverage (checked November 14, 2026): we are citing Nedap's official discontinuation page.

Related: [Apps and devices that stop working Jan 1, 2027](../../guides/apps-and-devices-that-stop-working-jan-1-2027/).

December 31, 2026. From that date you cannot log in, see energy data online, or run remote software updates. Nedap's official notice, fetched November 14, 2026, is the source.
Will the PowerRouter unit itself still work?
The local functions, including the integrated screen, remain unchanged. What ends is the website, remote updates, and all remaining Nedap support for the product line.
What should I do before December 31?
Save any energy data or records you still need. If you have a warranty issue, submit it in writing before that date; new claims will not be accepted afterward.

what:
Runna, the running-coaching app owned by Strava, is raising its UK prices. The company's own support page, [Changes to our UK subscription](https://support.runna.com/en/articles/18298149-changes-to-our-uk-subscription), fetched November 14, 2026, lists the new rates and when they apply.

## The new UK prices

The support page says:

- "Monthly subscription price: £15.99 > £17.99"
- "Annual subscription price: £99.99 > £109.99"
- "Strava + Runna annual subscription price: £119.99 > £124.99*"

The footnote on the bundle is: "This increase reflects Runna’s new price. The Strava price within the combined subscription remains the same." The annual plan is still the cheaper way to pay: twelve months at £17.99 comes to £215.88, against £109.99 paid upfront.

Runna's [UK pricing page](https://www.runna.com/en-gb/pricing), also fetched November 14, 2026, already shows the new UK rates of £17.99 a month and £109.99 a year, which matches the support page's rule for new subscribers.

## When you pay the new price

"For existing Runna subscribers: the new prices apply from your first renewal on or after 10 December, 2026. We’ll email you on 10 November to let you know." "For new Runna subscribers: the new prices apply from 10 November, 2026." What you have already paid stays at the old price until that renewal. The support page does not say you can avoid the rise by switching plan; new sign-ups and plan changes have already been on the new rates since November 10.

## US and other countries

The notice is titled "Changes to our UK subscription" and talks only about "users in the UK." Runna has not published a matching notice for other countries. The same pricing pages still list $19.99 a month and $119.99 a year among their currency prices (the default US dollar pair on [runna.com/pricing](https://www.runna.com/pricing) and the UK page, fetched November 14, 2026). We found no official US price change.

Coverage (checked November 14, 2026): [the5krunner](https://the5krunner.com/2026/11/10/quick-read-runna-price-rise/) reported the rise on November 10, including the bundle figure, which Runna's support page now confirms.

faq: When do Runna's UK prices go up?

For existing subscribers, at the first renewal on or after December 10, 2026. New UK subscribers have already been paying the new prices since November 10, 2026. That is from Runna's official support page, fetched November 14, 2026.
How much does Runna cost in the UK now?
£17.99 a month or £109.99 a year for new subscribers and anyone changing plan, up from £15.99 and £99.99. The Strava + Runna annual bundle goes from £119.99 to £124.99.
Is Runna going up in the US too?
Not that Runna has announced. The official notice is UK-only, and its pricing pages still list $19.99 a month and $119.99 a year.
